simple.meaning: קָשָׁה (qâshâh) appears 28 times in the Hebrew Scriptures and is introduced in connection with kingship. The surrounding account also brings the name into death.
simple.biblicalBackground: The first appearances are in Genesis, Exodus, Deuteronomy, 1 Samuel, 2 Samuel, and 9 more, beginning at Genesis 35:16. BibleIQ detects the main surrounding context as birth, family line, firstborn, sacrifice, death, kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to קָשָׁה (H7185) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: People in Scripture are understood by their place in the story. BibleIQ follows קָשָׁה through the actual verses so the reader sees the person in context instead of as an isolated dictionary entry.
simple.summary: קָשָׁה (qâshâh) / H7185 is tracked through Genesis 35:16, Genesis 35:17, Genesis 49:7, Exodus 7:3. The entry is generated from source alignment, occurrence evidence, and the surrounding Scripture context.

timeline.evidenceText: They traveled from Bethel. There was still some distance to come to Ephrath, and Rachel travailed. She had hard labor.
When she was in hard labor, the midwife said to her, “Don’t be afraid, for now you will have another son.”
Cursed be their anger, for it was fierce;
I will harden Pharaoh’s heart, and multiply my signs and my wonders in the land of Egypt.

When Pharaoh stubbornly refused to let us go, Yahweh killed all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, both the firstborn of man, and the firstborn of livestock. Therefore I sacrifice to Yahweh all that opens the womb, being males; but all the firstborn of my sons I redeem.’

You shall not show partiality in judgment; you shall hear the small and the great alike. You shall not be afraid of the face of man, for the judgment is God’s. The case that is too hard for you, you shall bring to me, and I will hear it.”
But Sihon king of Heshbon would not let us pass by him; for Yahweh your God hardened his spirit and made his heart obstinate, that he might deliver him into your hand, as it is today.
Circumcise therefore the foreskin of your heart, and be no more stiff-necked.
It shall not seem hard to you when you let him go free from you; for he has been double the value of a hired hand as he served you six years. Yahweh your God will bless you in all that you do.
When the men of Ashdod saw that it was so, they said, “The ark of the God of Israel shall not stay with us, for his hand is severe on us and on Dagon our god.”
“Your father made our yoke difficult. Now therefore make the hard service of your father, and his heavy yoke which he put on us, lighter, and we will serve you.”
He said, “You have asked a hard thing. If you see me when I am taken from you, it will be so for you; but if not, it will not be so.”
Notwithstanding, they would not listen, but hardened their neck, like the neck of their fathers, who didn’t believe in Yahweh their God.
“Your father made our yoke grievous: now therefore make the grievous service of your father, and his heavy yoke which he put on us, lighter, and we will serve you.”

Now don’t be stiff-necked, as your fathers were, but yield yourselves to Yahweh, and enter into his sanctuary, which he has sanctified forever, and serve Yahweh your God, that his fierce anger may turn away from you.
He also rebelled against king Nebuchadnezzar, who had made him swear by God; but he stiffened his neck, and hardened his heart against turning to Yahweh, the God of Israel.
“But they and our fathers behaved proudly, hardened their neck, didn’t listen to your commandments,

and refused to obey. They weren’t mindful of your wonders that you did among them, but hardened their neck, and in their rebellion appointed a captain to return to their bondage. But you are a God ready to pardon, gracious and merciful, slow to anger, and abundant in loving kindness, and didn’t forsake them.

and testified against them, that you might bring them again to your law. Yet they were arrogant, and didn’t listen to your commandments, but sinned against your ordinances (which if a man does, he shall live in them), turned their backs, stiffened their neck, and would not hear.

definitions.short: properly, to be dense , i.e. tough or severe (in various applications)
definitions.usage: be cruel, be fiercer, make grievous, be ((ask a), be in, have, seem, would) hard(-en, (labour), -ly, thing), be sore, (be, make) stiff(-en, (-necked)).
definitions.full: H7185. qashah I. [ קָשָׁה ] verb be hard, severe, fierce (Late Hebrew קָשָׁה be severe ; Arabic () be hard, dry , III. endure, struggle against, severity ; Aramaic קְשָׁא , be hard, difficult ; Jewish-Aramaic קַשְׁיָה קְשִׁי, adjective hard ); — Qal Perfect 3feminine singular קָֽשְׁתָה 1Sam 5:7 , קָשָׁ֑תָה Gen 49:7 ; Imperfect 3masculine singular יִקְשֶׁה Deut 1:17 ; 15:18 , וַיִּ֫קֶשׁ 2 Samuel 19:44; — 1 be hard, difficult Deut 1:17 (of a legal case; מִן comparative). 2 be hard, severe , עָלֵינוּ ׳ק יָדוֺ 1Sam 5:7 (of ׳י , in judgement); ׳יִק בְעֵינֶ֑ךָ . Deut 15:18 it shall not be hard in thine eyes (seem a severe trial, an injustice); of wrath Gen 49:7 (poem in J; || עָ֑ז ); of fierce words 2 Samuel 19:44. Niph`al Participle נִקְשֶׁה Isa 8:21 hardly bestead, hard pressed. Pi`el Imperfect 3feminine singular בְּלִדְתָּהּ וַתְּקַשׁ Gen 35:16 (E) she made hard in her bearing (had severe labour). Hiph`il Perfect 3masculine singular הִקְשָׁה Exod 13:15 +, etc.; Imperfect 3masculine singular וַיֶּקֶשׁ 2Chr 36:13 ; 3 masculine plural וַיַּקְשׁוּ Jer 7:26 +, etc.; Infinitive construct suffix בְּהַקְשֹׁתָהּ Gen 35:17 ; Participle מַקְשֶׁה Prov 28:14 ; 29:1 ; — 1 make difficult, difficulty: לְשַׁלְּחֵנוּ הִקְשָׁה Exod 13:15 Pharaoh made difficulty about sending us away ; of travail Gen 35:17 (E; as Pi`el ); לִשְׁאוֺל הִקְשִׁיתָ 2Kin 2:10 thou hast made hard to ask , asked a hard thing. 2 make severe, burdensome , yoke imposed by king 1Kin 12:4 2Chr 10:4 . 3. a. make hard, stiff, stubborn , figurative of obstinacy: אֶתעָֿרְמָּם וַיַּקְשׁוּ 2Kin 17:14 they stiffened their neck , so Jer 7:26 ; 17:23 ; 19:15 ; Deut 10:16 ; 2Chr 30:8 ; 36:13 ; Neh 9:16-17 , 29 ; Prov 29:1 ; לְבַבְכֶם אַלתַּֿקְשׁוּ Psa 95:8 , compare Prov 28:14 ; subject פ אֶתלֵֿב ׳אַקְשֶׁה ׳י, Exod 7:3 (P), accusative אֶתרֿוחוֺ Deut 2:30 , b. shew stubborness Job 9:4 (with אֶל person [ ׳י ]).
